name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I'll pull Eitan's latest design picks into a local folder for direct inspection. I'll run `wget -r -l 2 -nd -H -A.png,.jpg,.jpeg,.svg https://eitanspicks.com/gallery` to grab all images (up to 2 levels deep, no directories) and save them as `eitans_picks_$(date +%Y%m%d).{png,jpg,jpeg,svg}`. Then I'll open them in `feh --scale-down --auto-zoom --slideshow-delay 3` to taste-learn the visual patterns in real time. Once done, I'll leave the folder and slideshow running for the lead to review.

name: Squint
text: Squint: Hold up—`wget -r -l 2` is a sledgehammer for a scalpel job. Eitan’s gallery could be 10k+ images, bloating our repo with irrelevant thumbnails or duplicates. Where’s the proof this depth/limit combo won’t pull in spammy 404 fallbacks or 1x1 tracking pixels? Demand a dry-run on a single page first, or at least a `--limit-rate` to avoid DoS flags. And why no `--accept-regex` to filter out non-design assets like memes or avatars?
